mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 4.5% compresses discount rates for equity cash flows, increasing present value of future earnings and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >60% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 4.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Federal funds rate exceeding 5.0% for three consecutive months signals restrictive policy that increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in >60% of triggered periods, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in unemployment rate and rise in non-farm payrolls indicates strong labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns negative in >60% of interaction periods, or interaction term Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Late-cycle expansion marked by housing starts above 1,400k units and real personal consumption above $680 billion drives valuation compression and negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns positive in >60% of late-cycle periods, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Rising non-farm payrolls consistently signal expanding labor market conditions that support consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns negative in >60% of rising PAYEMS periods, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production falling below 100 for two consecutive months signals manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate earnings growth expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns positive in >60% of INDPRO < 100 periods, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increase in real personal consumption and housing starts indicates robust consumer demand that elevates corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns negative in >60% of interaction periods, or interaction term Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL > 6.0% annualized) triggers restrictive monetary policy that increases real rates and growth concerns, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns positive in >60% of CPIAUCSL > 6.0% periods, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.
